narrative: Your law school application was denied because the model predicted a 72.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. The strongest factor driving this prediction was your third-year class rank: you were in the first decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. That very low rank pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 39, which is above the accepted student average of about 37, so it actually pushed toward passing. However, your first-year decile of 2—well below the accepted average of 6—was the third most important factor and also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.90 is below the accepted average of 3.23, though it was not among the top three drivers. To improve your chances in a future application, focus on raising your academic performance record, consider retaking the LSAT to strengthen that already positive signal, and address the weak third-year ranking directly in your personal statement. You may also pursue a post-baccalaureate program to demonstrate readiness for law school.
